title: Codex on Windows Gets an MXC Sandbox With No Admin Setup: Check If Your PC Supports It
key_facts: OpenAI announced a new Codex sandbox mode on 9 Oct 2026, built on Microsoft Execution Containers (MXC), for compatible Windows 11 PCs.
It needs no administrator-approved setup and adds neither separate Windows accounts nor local firewall rules.
OpenAI cites faster setup, stronger network enforcement and finer control over file access.
The sandbox applies the active file and network permissions to a command and its child processes.
Microsoft introduced Process Isolation for MXC on 27 Aug 2026 and said MXC was generally available on 7 Oct 2026.
Codex CLI 0.162.0 or later can test MXC support; a success prints MXC_OK. The ChatGPT desktop app prefers MXC when the device supports it; an organisation can block it with allow_mxc = false.
A bug report opened 4 Oct 2026 describes MXC stopping before a command starts because an unrelated BitLocker drive is locked; other users added matching failures and it was open on 9 Oct.
Codex can run on recent, fully updated Windows 10 on a best-effort basis, but that does not establish MXC availability.
quote_evidence: Codex on Windows has a new sandbox mode built on Microsoft Execution Containers (MXC) for compatible Windows 11 PCs.
It needs no administrator-approved setup and adds neither separate Windows accounts nor local firewall rules.
MXC changes how Windows enforces those boundaries; it does not give a command unrestricted access to your PC.
why_it_matters_hint: Developers on compatible Windows 11 PCs can limit what an AI coding agent may touch without administrator setup.
notes: Outlet relays OpenAI's announcement (quoted post) and OpenAI's documentation; BitLocker bug is a user report, not confirmed by OpenAI.
